timeline.event: Renewcell, developer of CIRCULOSE and operator of the Ortviken plant in Sundsvall, Sweden, was declared bankrupt in February.
The investment firm Altor acquired the remaining business and plant later that year, and the company was renamed Circulose after its product.
Circulose announced in September that it would trace material from pulp to garment through TextileGenesis.
In December Circulose announced a partner-only model under which pulp is available only to brands with direct partnerships.
Circulose announced in February, with commitments from 11 brands, that it planned to restart production at Ortviken in the fourth quarter of 2026.

timeline.event: DuPont commercialized Sorona poly(trimethylene terephthalate), using 1,3-propanediol from corn-sugar fermentation.
The FTC adopted triexta as a US generic name for a polyester subclass based on 1,3-propanediol, covering PTT.
DuPont agreed to sell its biomaterials business, including Sorona, to Huafon Group for about 240 million dollars.
The sale closed and the business relaunched as Covation Biomaterials.

timeline.event: DuPont chemists, including Joseph Shivers, developed spandex, the segmented polyurethane fiber later sold as LYCRA, according to a fabric-industry history.
Shandong Ruyi completed its purchase of The LYCRA Company in January.
Lenders took control of The LYCRA Company after the Shandong Ruyi purchase ended in default.
The LYCRA Company filed a prepackaged Chapter 11 case in the Southern District of Texas on 17 March and emerged on 20 May with more than 1.2 billion dollars of debt eliminated.
